classification.difficultyReason: Use the tangent-radius right angle to identify an exact central angle from tangent, then substitute it into the sector-area formula.

content.prompt: A circle of radius $1$ and centre $O$ is drawn below. The line segment $AC$ is tangent to the circle, and $B$ is the point of intersection of $OC$ with the circle. Find the area of the shaded region shown in the figure below.

spec.description: Circle centred at O, with vertical radius OA, horizontal tangent AC, and segment OC meeting the circle at B. The minor sector AOB is shaded.
spec.mathematics: OA=1, AC=sqrt(3), OA perpendicular to AC, O-B-C collinear. Coordinates derive from O=(0,0), A=(0,1), C=(sqrt(3),1), and OB=1.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear; the central angle and sector area are not supplied.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ square units.

Use $\tan\angle AOB=\sqrt{3}$ to find the central angle, then apply $A=\tfrac12r^2\theta$.
answer.worked:
The radius is perpendicular to the tangent, so $\angle OAC=90^\circ$. Let $\theta=\angle AOB=\angle AOC$.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{AC}{OA}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{1}\\\theta&=\frac{\pi}{3}.\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12r^2\theta\\A&=\frac12\times1^2\times\frac{\pi}{3}\\A&=\frac{\pi}{6}\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$
